newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat exports jump in July-December, HGCA says. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UK wheat exports jump in July-December, HGCA says. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]

text.p: The UK exported 2,435,622 tonnes of wheat in July to December 1996, compared with 1,717,049 tonnes in the same period in 1995, the Home Grown Cereals Authority said.
This figure "is well above the corresponding totals for the past three years, reflecting the strong pace of exports this season," the HGCA said in its Weekly Digest.
Of the total some 1.8 million tonnes went to other EU destinations, representing a 28 percent increase, despite record crops in many EU countries.
"Low domestic prices in the UK following the record harvest and relatively firm EU prices meant that UK exports were very competitive during this period," the HGCA said.
Exports to non-EU destinations had more than doubled over the same period, "largely due to the commission's more aggressive export programme," it said.
Latest ministry figures put export availability at 4.2 million tonnes, but the HGCA said that more recent trade estimates were in the range 3.7 to 4.2 million tonnes.

Given, however, that animal feed usage may be lower than the ministry estimates, "it seems unlikely (corrects from likely) that the export availability is significantly below four million tonnes," the HGCA said.

"Recent trade reports suggest end-March exports could be in the range of 3.4 to 3.5 million tonnes," the HGCA said. "This means that there could still be 0.5 to 0.8 million tonnes left for export in the final three months of this season."
"In the past three years exports of UK wheat in the last three months have been between 0.5 and 0.75 million tonnes," the HGCA said.
Barley exports in July to December were recorded as 1.3 million tonnes, an increase of 39 percent on the total for the same period in 1995.

The rise is despite a fall of 200,000 tonnes in exports to other EU destinations, especially to Spain, where a recovery in production has lowered import requirements. Exports to non-EU countries have risen on increased demand and a more aggressive EU export policy, the HGCA said, citing increased Saudi Arabian purchases in particular.

"An active export programme since December suggests that most of the estimated 2.3 million tonne UK barley export availability should be absorbed, leaving little scope for any large intervention offers at the end of the season," the HGCA said. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
